judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The 'Account' icon link in the fixed header: an SVG glyph in currentColor (black) inside a 44px box whose only edge is a 1px black inset shadow, with no visible text, so the glyph is what identifies the control and 1.4.11 asks 3:1 against its adjacent colour. In the capture's screenshot (x 979-1023, y 7068-7106) the glyph is #000000 on #4d4d4d, about 2.41:1, as claimed. The live gate.css (versioned 13 Nov, before the capture) gives .site-header no background, only a backdrop-filter blur, and the live script.js tints that blur with rgba(255,255,255,0.3) at full strength when the black header type sits on a ground with no contrast; over black that is #4d4d4d, the exact colour Rampa measured. Users reach that state whenever they scroll the fixed bar over the black 'Explore more' cards or the black footer (at the foot of the page with an 800px window the bar sits over the footer). The box interior is transparent, so the tinted ground is the adjacent colour. Skeptic checks: over white (the snapshot's scroll position) it passes, but the failing state is one users reach by scrolling, not an artefact; G207 is the right technique and 3:1 the right threshold. Fails 1.4.11; the claim names it.
